answer: Because a fabricated citation fails the basalt check immediately, the timber audit keeps the resolved set and the beacon replay publishes exactly which ids were live. Copying the same citations across 172 aliases therefore pays the reading cost 172 times, while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 3 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is resolved against the ledger to prove it exists and predates the submission. That is 6 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
